category: Classical Seven Wonders of the Ancient World
explanation: The first four items are traditionally listed as four of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. The Parthenon, while a significant ancient structure, is not part of that classical list.
Zeus, Poseidon, Hera, and Hades are major deities from Greek mythology. Jupiter is the Roman equivalent of Zeus, making it the odd one out as a Roman deity among Greek ones.

The words 'Evil', 'Veil', 'Vile', and 'Live' are all anagrams of each other, using the letters L, I, V, E. 'Love' uses a different set of letters (L, O, V, E) and therefore is not an anagram of 'Live' or the other words.
